name: Methionine
short: Review: a mistaken 10-fold overdose was fatal; high intakes impaired infant growth; methionine worsens symptoms in schizophrenia. Loading test in 887 people: dizziness common, no deaths.
text: A review of methionine toxicity in humans reports that a dose 10 times larger than the standard methionine loading dose (0.1 g/kg), given by mistake, resulted in death; that methionine is known to make psychiatric symptoms worse in people with schizophrenia, with no evidence of similar effects in healthy people; that intakes higher than 5 times normal raised homocysteine levels; and that in infants, intakes 2 to 5 times normal impaired growth and caused extremely high blood methionine levels, although no adverse long-term consequences were observed. The same review states that nutritional and metabolic studies using amounts below and above the requirement have not reported adverse effects in adults and children, and that the standard loading dose causes acute vascular dysfunction that is unlikely to cause permanent damage. In a study of 887 people (296 with coronary or peripheral arterial disease and 591 controls) given the standard L-methionine loading test (100 mg/kg), acute complications occurred in 33% of women and 16.5% of men; dizziness was the most common and was attributed to methionine, and sleepiness, nausea, passing large amounts of urine (polyuria) and raised or lowered blood pressure were also seen; none died within 30 days, and the authors described the complications as transitory but impairing perception and vigilance. The abstracts do not state the route. No interaction data with medicines were found in the cited sources.
